newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London dived to a 31-month-low towards the close pounded by speculative and fund long liquidation. Traders noted follow-through sales in the afternoon after benchmark January failed to come back towards the previous $1,360 support. The second position January plunged to an intraday low of $1,349 a tonne, the lowest level since April 15, 1994, when it touched $1,347. At the close, January stood at $1,352, a loss of $38. New support is now seen at $1,315. Spot month November also lost further ground, falling by a sharp $67 to $1,353 as longs liquidated some of their positions before the November expiry on Friday. The sharp decline helped wipe out November's recent hefty premium to January. January/March switches saw deals at around $40. The CSCE in New York was closed for the Thanksgiving Holiday.

COLOMBIA - Colombia's National Federation of Coffee Growers announced registrations for November coffee shipments by private exporters would close November 29. In a brief statement the organization said registration for January and February shipments by private and Federation exporters would open December 2. Private exporters will be authorized to ship 1.620 million 60-kg bags in January through March, and Federation exporters will be allowed to ship 1.080 million bags, according to the statement.

POLAND - Coffee imports in June 1996 amounted to 114,958 bags, up on last year's 97,942 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996 (January/June) up to 782,100 bags, 3.7 per cent up on last year's 754,112 bags. Total imports in 1995 reached 1.536 million bags against 1.442 million bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Indonesia (142,800 vs 95,500 bags), Vietnam (125,200 vs 148,900 bags) and India (95,900 vs 44,000 bags).

CANADA - Coffee imports in August 1996 reached 240,165 bags, up on last year's 183,179 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first eight months of 1996 (January/August) up to 1.817 million bags, 15 per cent more than in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 2.510 million bags against 2.827 million bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Colombia (317,200 vs 230,300 bags), Mexico (215,800 vs 107,700 bags), Guatemala (161,000 vs 145,600 bags) and Brazil (111,800 vs 162,400 bags). The USA continued to be the largest supplier of roast and ground coffee delivering 259,200 bags compared to 243,500 bags. Coffee exports in August 1996 reached 26,970 bags, up from last year's 20,634 bags. This brought cumulative exports in January/August 1996 up to 206,366 bags, 8.3 per cent up on the 190,610 bags imported in January/August 1995. Canada exports most of its coffee in the form of solubles with the USA (144,800 vs 148,300 bags) being the main market.
